what_happened: Job 20261031-230912-n9tm ("use GitHub CI result for the candidate in the checks stage") ended failed. Admission refused the change because crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs adds an email address outside the allow-list. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet, no checks failed, and no findings were raised. The work was refused at admission and not judged.
cause: The admission allow-list for email-like text is enforced only at admission, after the producer has written the code. The producer, and the reading and plan that guide it, are not shown the rule. Nothing scans the planned or produced diff for email-like literals (a git author or bot identity in a new GitHub client path) before dispatch or before the job is submitted. The class was already known, but no earlier case closed the gap. The rule stays invisible to the writer, so a CI-related change that needs a git or bot identity breaks it.
prevention: Run the admission allow-list scan on the producer's working diff during the producer stage, and again as a pre-commit step inside the job. On a hit, feed the offending file and line back to the producer for repair within the same run. Also put the rule in the producer brief: no email-like literals in code outside the allow-list. Take identities from config or from git's own settings, or build them without an at-sign literal.
proposed_request: Re-run job 20261031-230912-n9tm: in the checks stage, use the GitHub CI result for the candidate. Do not write any email address or email-like literal, such as a git author or bot identity, into code outside the admission allow-list. In crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs, take any identity from existing config or from git's own settings. Before the job finishes, run the same email allow-list scan that admission runs on the diff, and fix any hit. Acceptance: admission accepts the diff, the existing checks pass, and the checks stage uses the CI result for the candidate branch as the earlier request described.
